_readme: Part catalog for the headless CAD/CAM CLI. 'recipes' say HOW to cut; 'parts' say WHICH file and which recipe. The cut list only needs to name a part key, a color and a qty. Every parameter below was read off an existing production .tap file — add new recipes the same way rather than guessing.

foam-2in.description: 2in XLPE foam, 1/4in bit, full depth in one pass. Matches CAD/XRT-50.tap.

foam-0.75-jig.description: 3/4in foam print jig, 1/2in bit, full depth in one pass. Matches CAD/20 piece male print jig - foam.tap.

ops._allowNested: The 20 MALE parts sit inside the LAYER_1 sheet boundary; CAD/20 piece male print jig - foam.tap cuts all 21 with this one outside profile, so the containment is parts-in-a-boundary, not holes.

foam-2in-holes.description: Same 2in foam cut as foam-2in, but interior holes get their own inside pass first so they come out on size. Use for any part with holes.

XRT-50.name: Rescue tube 50in
XRT-50._note: This DXF is already a laid-out 49 x 95.9 sheet of 16 tubes, so batch cuts it as-is instead of nesting it.

print-jig-20.file: CAD/20 piece male print jig - foam.dxf
print-jig-20._note: Already laid out as a 37 x 29.8 jig sheet of 21 shapes.

add a single part._: Leave out 'prenested' when the file holds ONE part — batch will nest it with the others by color.

a part with holes._: Holes must be cut with their own inside op, or an outside profile makes them a tool-diameter too big. Put the holes on their own DXF layer and give the recipe two ops:
a part with holes.__: Ops run in order and post into ONE .tap with tool changes. Interior work first; the outside profile that frees the part goes last. 'optional' lets the op be skipped when a part has no such layer. The CLI warns if it sees nested contours and no inside op.

_howto.not yet catalogued: The LGC 50 chair boards in CAD/ are multi-tool wood jobs (T8 + T3, layers like T9_COUNTERSINK_0_6 and T3_PROFILE_INSIDE_2). Their layer-to-operation mapping needs to be confirmed before a recipe is written for them.

parametric parts._: A part with a 'shape' instead of a 'file' is generated on the fly, so one entry covers every size. The cut list's size column ('20x10', '24 x 18', '48') sets the dimensions; put w/h in the shape spec to fix a default when a row has no size.
parametric parts.kinds: rect · roundrect (r) · capsule · circle (d) · ellipse · polygon (sides) · star (points, innerRatio)
parametric parts.holes: shape.holes takes {kind:'circle',x,y,d}, {kind:'rect',x,y,w,h} or {kind:'grid',cols,rows,d,margin}. Holes land on the HOLES layer and the outline on OUTLINE, so foam-2in-holes cuts them correctly with no extra work.
parametric parts.your SKUs: Add entries keyed by the SKU your cut list actually uses, pointing at the same shape spec — e.g. an AM-SC-KX entry with shape {kind:'roundrect', r:2}. The keys above are generic templates.
parametric parts.one-off: No catalog entry needed for a one-off: node cam-engine/cli.js cut --shape roundrect --size 20x10 --recipe foam-2in --out part.tap

_lgc_analysis._: Why the LGC boards are catalogued as existing machine files rather than regenerating recipes. Derived by parsing each .tap and matching its toolpaths back to the .dxf geometry.

what each tap actually does.Board 1, 2, 5: T8 @ S10000, plunge F20: drills through at 1.5in, at the centroids of the ~0.375in closed shapes. Then T3 @ S18000, plunge F20 / cut F60: cuts the 4 OPEN 2-point crosscut lines ON the line, 1.5in deep in 0.375in passes, with one tab per line (Z lifts to -1.375, so a 0.125in tab).
what each tap actually does.Board 3: T8, T3, T9, T3 — adds a T9 op between two T3 ops.
what each tap actually does.Board 4: T10 drill to 0.5in, T5 @ S20000 F25 to 0.1in, T8 drill to 1.5in, T3 to 0.5in, T9 to 0.5in, then T3 crosscuts to 1.5in. Six ops.

why not a recipe: The taps cut a SELECTED SUBSET of the dxf. Board 1's dxf carries pocket and countersink geometry (T9-T3_POCKET, the larger T9_COUNTERSINK_0_6 shapes) and a full 3.5x97 board outline on T3_PROFILE_INSIDE_2 that its tap never touches. A recipe that cut by layer would cut geometry Dan deliberately left alone.

The selection crosses layers rather than following them: the 8 drilled holes sit on REAR_LEG, FRONT_LEG, PART_P and T9_COUNTERSINK_0_6 alike, selected by being small closed shapes, not by layer. The 4 crosscuts are the only OPEN shapes, again spanning three layers.
Each board runs a different op sequence (2, 4 and 6 ops), so there is no single LGC recipe.
The crosscuts carry tabs on OPEN contours. camcore's profileOp only tabs CLOSED contours, so a regenerated toolpath would drop those tabs and the offcuts would come loose mid-cut.
_lgc_analysis.to convert one to a recipe later: The engine would need a geometry selector beyond layers (open-vs-closed plus a size band) and tab support on open contours. Until then the existing .tap files are both correct and already proven on the machine.
